neighbours.label: ' where' introducing a relative or contrast clause ('her third flight where she was commander', 'whereas')
fire: She returned to space on her third flight, where she served as commander.
The town had many workshops, where tanners and weavers found steady work.
They moved to a small village in Wales, where he wrote his last novel.
The body was dressed as if alive, whereas a corpse normally looks pale.
We visited the old harbor, where fishing boats unload every morning.
He joined the air force under another name, where he trained new pilots.
The seeds were sent to a lab in Utah, where they were tested for disease.
Turn left at the church, where the road splits into two lanes.
